messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Kiet's eyes would lock onto the horizon, scanning for any sign of trouble as he navigated his fishing boat through the choppy waters of the Gulf. It had been three years since his son, Linh, was lost at sea during a routine fishing trip. Kiet was certain that if only he had been more vigilant, more cautious, Linh would still be alive today. This guilt gnawed at him, making him feel dead inside – as though all joy and warmth had been extinguished. As the days turned into weeks, and the weeks into months, Kiet began to notice changes in himself. He was always on edge, his senses heightened, waiting for the other shoe to drop. The sound of seagulls would send a shiver down his spine, reminding him of that fateful day when Linh didn't return. His sleep became fitful and erratic – he'd lie awake at night, replaying every moment leading up to Linh's disappearance, wondering what he could've done differently. Kiet's mistrust of others grew as well; he couldn't shake the feeling that people were hiding something from him. He'd become withdrawn, pushing away his friends and family – even his wife, Tuyet. She tried to be supportive, but Kiet just felt like she didn't understand what he was going through. As the months passed, these physical reactions intensified – his heart racing whenever he saw a boat in distress or heard the sound of waves crashing against the shore. He'd become convinced that every wave held some hidden danger, waiting to snatch away someone else he loved. This fear fueled his hypervigilance, making him even more prone to jump at every little thing. His emotional numbness made it hard for Kiet to connect with others – or even himself. He'd go through the motions of daily life without any sense of purpose or meaning. His relationships began to fray; Tuyet would try to talk to him about Linh, but he just couldn't bear it. It was as if speaking his son's name out loud would unleash a torrent of emotions he wasn't prepared to face. One day, while Kiet was out fishing, a sudden storm rolled in – the same kind that had claimed Linh's life. As the winds howled and lightning flashed across the sky, Kiet felt himself transported back to that terrible night. His body went into overdrive – his heart racing, his senses on high alert. In that moment, all his worst fears came flooding back: the thought of losing Tuyet or someone else he cared about; the feeling of being powerless against nature's fury. Kiet returned home that evening, shaken to his core. He knew then that he couldn't keep going on like this – something had to give. It was time for him to face his demons head-on and work through the guilt, mistrust, and emotional numbness that had taken hold of his life. With a newfound sense of determination, Kiet decided it was time to seek help – before his memories consumed him completely.
